title: Marker-free genome editing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae using CRISPR-Cas9
author: Hemani, Grissom, et al.

steps.title: Prepare media plates
steps.instruction: Prepare YPD, SC‑URA, and 5‑FOA agar plates at least 2 days before use to allow adequate drying.

steps.title: Prepare transformation reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh LiOAc‑TE solution and 40 % PEG3350; replace if older than 3 months because degradation reduces transformation efficiency.

steps.title: Implement safety precautions
steps.instruction: Handle chloroform and 5‑FOA in a certified fume hood while wearing gloves, lab coat, and safety goggles; dispose of waste according to institutional policy.

steps.title: Isolate genomic DNA for PCR
steps.instruction: Extract high‑quality yeast genomic DNA suitable for PCR verification of marker removal.

substeps.instruction: a. Transfer a single yeast colony (prepare 8–10 colonies total) from an agar plate to 5 mL YPD medium using a sterile applicator.
b. Incubate at 30 °C with shaking at 200–250 rpm for 14–16 h to reach stationary phase.
c. Harvest cells by centrifuging the culture at ~2,000 × g for 4 min; discard supernatant.
d. Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL sterile ultrapure H₂O.
e. Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
f. Centrifuge at ~5,000 × g for 1 min and aspirate the supernatant.
g. Resuspend the pellet in 250 µL lysis buffer.
i. Add acid‑washed glass beads until the liquid level reaches the 500 µL mark (zirc­onia beads 425–600 µm may substitute).
ii. Vortex vigorously at maximum speed for 15 min to disrupt cells.
iii. Add 150 µL 7.5 M ammonium acetate (pH 7.0) and mix thoroughly.
iv. Incubate at 65 °C for 15 min.
h. Place the tube on ice for 15 min.
i. Add 500 µL chloroform, gently invert several times to mix (exercise caution to avoid leakage).
j. Centrifuge at ~5,000 × g for 5 min.
k. Transfer the upper aqueous layer to a new microcentrifuge tube, avoiding the interphase.
l. (Repeat steps a–k as needed).
m. Precipitate DNA by adding 500 µL 100 % isopropanol and mix gently.
n. Centrifuge at ~5,000 × g for 5 min to pellet DNA.
o. Discard supernatant and wash the pellet with 500 µL 70 % ethanol without disturbing it.
p. Centrifuge again at ~5,000 × g for 5 min.
q. Discard supernatant, spin the tube 5–10 s to collect residual liquid, and pipette off any remaining ethanol.
r. Air‑dry the pellet with caps open in a 30 °C incubator for 5–10 min.
s. Resuspend the dried DNA pellet in 50 µL TE buffer.
t. Verify DNA concentration and purity using spectrophotometry or an equivalent method.
